newsitem.title: USA: Union to take Q4 charge, cut positions.
newsitem.headline: Union to take Q4 charge, cut positions.

text.p: Union Camp Corp said on Monday it will take a special, non-recurring pre-tax charge in the fourth quarter of $47 million for restructuring charges and asset write-downs.
The charge will reduce 1996 after-tax net income by about $29 million, or $0.42 per share, the company said.
The charge is part of a restructuring program which includes a goal to add as much as $100 million to the company's pre-tax earning power over the next 18 to 24 months.
Also part of the program is the elimination of about 400 positions in various operational and staff functions, Union Camp said.
"The paper industry is changing, and Union Camp is moving aggressively to capitalize on these changes," said W. Craig McClelland, chairman and chief executive.

"The capital intensive nature of this industry, that is operating in a global marketplace of low to moderate economic growth and inflation, requires that we be even more disciplined in the future regarding cost control, asset returns and targeted growth," he said.
The company said it expects about two-thirds of the $100 million of added earning power to come from cost reductions and asset realignments.
For the employees cut, the company said it would offer an enhanced severance package. The workforce reductions will be implemented mostly over the next nine months, Union Camp said.

The company said it plans to focus its ongoing programs to improve profitability on product and business mix shifts and aggressive marketing investments. It also said it would realign portions of its assets.
Union Camp posted 1995 sales of $4.2 billion.
